GELINA, 150 MeV Geel pulsed electron
linear accelerator, Electron burst width 1 nanosec,
repetition rate 100 Hz,
Initial neutrons produced by (gamma,n) and
(gamma,fis) reactions induced via Bremsstrahlung
from the electron beam hitting a rotating uranium
target, which was cooled by mercury.
Fast neutron from the target moderated to a
white spectrum by water contained in beryllium
canning of 4.0cm thick walls situated above uranium
target
GELINA Flight path number 2; angle of the flight
path with respect to the electron beam is 279 degree.
.White Neutron Source. The neutron energy is derived
from the measured time-of-flight using expression -
--EN(eV)=(72.298*L/TOF)**2 with L=26.443 m and TOF
in microseconds. Cd overlap filter, gamma flash was
reduced by 5 mm Pb, background points were determined
with black resonance technique using Cd, Au, and Co
filters. The background was deduced from a fit of the
background points with a power function using AGS.
Neutrons detected at 26.443+/-0.002 m
with a 110 mm diameter and 12.7 mm thick Li-6 glass
(NE912),scintillator viewed by two 5-inch PMT placed
orthogonal to the neutron beam
Dead-time interval was monitored electronically and
measured as 1130 ns.
BF3 monitors were mounted in the ceiling of
target hall.  For neutron beam intensity monitoring.
The transmission factor is obtained from dead time
and background corrected yields.
Cylindrical PuO2 powder mixed with graphite in copper
container, purity  of Pu-242 = 99.93%, diam. 6.5 cm,
thickness = 2.51E-05 atoms/barn, sample out posi-
tion with graphite in Cu-container placed at approx.
10 m from the neutron source.The sample temperature
was kept by a cryostatic sample holder at temperatures
of 12 K , 77 K and 300 K.
The sample was positioned in and out of the beam with
an automatic sample changer. Cycle time 10 min.
Dummies consisted of the same amount of graphite powder
Corrections were made for:
* Dead time
* Background based on Cd, Au, and Co black resonances
(see INC-SPECT)
